prose.title: C-Town Chivalry Let Two Big Salaries Go and Bought Better Ones
prose.dek: Bear Dunn released George Pickens and Tony Pollard on the day the auction roster locked, then spent {{f.team.0009.faa_spend}} on Christian McCaffrey, Joe Burrow and more. The preseason simulation ranks C-Town {{f.team.0009.power_rank|ord}}, with the league's best title odds at {{f.team.0009.sim_p_title}}.

paragraphs: Dunn started the offseason with the best roster in the league and knew it. In April he had {{f.team.0009.active_roster_opening}} active players and {{f.team.0009.cap_opening}} in salary, and {{f.team.0009.studs_opening}} top-twelve starters: Jayden Daniels at quarterback, James Cook at running back, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, an Elite WR1, and Drake London at receiver, Brock Bowers, an Elite TE1, and Sam LaPorta in the superflex. Breece Hall and Tee Higgins were solid behind them. The one hole was Tony Pollard, a Low-end RB3, in the second flex.

Before the draft he kept it simple. LaPorta's rookie deal was running out, so Dunn extended him in May at {{f.team.0009.contract_16214_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0009.contract_16214_tcv}} in all. The other three expiring rookies, Hendon Hooker, Jake Haener and Jonathan Mingo, were let go. He cut Dyami Brown, whose {{f.team.0009.cut_15292_salary}} salary cost a {{f.team.0009.cut_15292_penalty}} penalty, and released Tyler Higbee for nothing. No trades.

t.0009.slot_bridge.title: April: who held each priced slot

paragraphs: The tag came first. In May Dunn tagged George Pickens at {{f.team.0009.tag_15762_salary}}, which is what a tag really is in this league: a chip. Keep the player, trade him, or hand him back before the auction and take the money with you. The draft was an afterthought, {{f.team.0009.rookie_picks_count}} late picks, both defenders, Caleb Downs at 4.09 and Jake Golday at 6.09, and he bought Brian Branch at the Expired Rookie Auction for {{f.team.0009.era_16244_price}}.

Then the week before the lock, everything moved. He extended James Cook at {{f.team.0009.contract_15715_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0009.contract_15715_tcv}} in all. In a three-way deal with Real Deal Creel and Blake Bombers he sent Drake London and {{f.team.0009.trade_blind_bid_cash}} of blind-bid money away and got Tetairoa McMillan back, shedding {{f.team.0009.trade1_salary_out}} of salary and taking on {{f.team.0009.trade1_salary_in}}. And on lock day he cashed the chip: Pickens was released with no penalty, all {{f.team.0009.cut_15762_salary}} straight back to him, and Tony Pollard went the same day, {{f.team.0009.cut_14085_salary}} of salary off the books with a {{f.team.0009.cut_14085_penalty}} penalty.

That is why the roster shrank before the auction, from {{f.team.0009.active_roster_opening}} active players in April to {{f.team.0009.active_roster_preauction}} at the lock, and the salary from {{f.team.0009.cap_opening}} to {{f.team.0009.cap_preauction}}. Brown, Higbee, Pollard and London went out, McMillan and Branch came in, and Pickens came and went. None of it was an accident: it was room for the auction.

t.0009.moves_s2.title: From the draft to the auction lock

paragraphs: The room was opened on purpose too. The Cook deal was restructured the same day it was signed, down to {{f.team.0009.contract_15715_salary_2}} for 2026 with the {{f.team.0009.contract_15715_tcv_2}} total untouched, and all of it got used. At the Free Agent Auction Dunn spent {{f.team.0009.faa_spend}} on {{f.team.0009.faa_lots_won}} players: Christian McCaffrey for {{f.team.0009.faa_13130_price}} after seventeen bids, Joe Burrow for {{f.team.0009.faa_14777_price}} and DK Metcalf for {{f.team.0009.faa_14102_price}}.

McCaffrey has a history this summer. Sex Manther tagged him in May and let him go in July, and Dunn paid barely more than that tag to get him. That is not a mistake by Josh Martel: the tag was his chip, and when he threw it back the money went back in his pocket to spend on other people.

What it bought is what separates C-Town from the rest of the league table. McCaffrey is a High-end RB1 and Burrow a High-end QB1, the two Very good buys in the What it bought column, and his offense gained more at the auction than anyone's, {{f.team.0009.faa_off_gain_rank|ord}} of {{f.league.teams}}, and ranked {{f.team.0009.faa_off_rank|ord}} for what each dollar added. Burrow's deal runs long, {{f.team.0009.contract_14777_salary}} this year and {{f.team.0009.contract_14777_tcv}} in all, one of {{f.team.0009.myac_faa}} multi-year contracts he handed out from the auction. After it he trimmed only depth, releasing Patrick Queen and three minimum bodies at no cost.

The lineup it built has {{f.team.0009.holes_today}} holes. The {{f.team.0009.studs_today}} top-twelve starters are Burrow, McCaffrey, Cook, Smith-Njigba, Bowers and Daniels in the superflex, with Higgins, Hall and McMillan solid around them. His backfield ranks {{f.team.0009.rb_rank|ord}} in the league, his quarterbacks {{f.team.0009.qb_rank|ord}}, his receivers {{f.team.0009.wr_rank|ord}} and his tight ends {{f.team.0009.te_rank|ord}}. The kicker, Jake Bates, is an Elite PK1 on MFL's projections, and the defense is the one thin spot, a footnote on a roster like this.

paragraphs: Dunn has been here since {{f.team.0009.hist_first_season}}, and the record has a gap in it that he would recognise. His teams have had the league's best all-play record {{f.team.0009.hist_ap_titles}} times, in {{f.team.0009.hist_ap_title_years}}, with {{f.team.0009.hist_div_titles}} division titles and {{f.team.0009.hist_playoffs}} playoff trips, but only one championship, in {{f.team.0009.hist_title_years}}. His career all-play record is {{f.team.0009.hist_allplay_pct}}.

DOG POUND 4 LIFE belongs to C-Town until someone takes it: Dunn has won it the last two years. The simulation gives him a {{f.team.0009.sim_p_division}} chance to make it three, {{f.team.0009.sim_p_playoffs}} playoff odds and {{f.team.0009.sim_p_bye}} odds of a bye. Cleon Ca$h is {{f.league.power_rank_0011|ord}} in the league and the Hawks {{f.league.power_rank_0012|ord}}, and C-Town plays each of them five times.

The next three years, told the way Dunn would tell them. 2027: C-Town won the division. Nobody was surprised. 2028: (In the voice of Morgan Freeman) He had the best roster in the league for a third straight year, and he had built it without saying much at all. 2029: They won the whole thing. It had been thirteen years. He posted one line about it and logged off.

Week one has started the way the summer went. With {{f.league.wk_teams_final}} NFL teams done, Smith-Njigba had a long touchdown and a big day, McCaffrey chipped in, and C-Town has {{f.team.0009.wk_points_final}} points in the bank.
